title: anomaly.sales.detected
description: One event per sales anomaly incident (an unusual spike or drop in daily sales of one product at one warehouse). Published by the anomaly-detection service batch job to the Kafka topic named after event_type (anomaly.sales.detected), partition key = payload.sku_id + '|' + payload.warehouse_id. The payload.date is the first day of the incident; later days of the same incident do not get their own event. Delivery is at-least-once: a crash replay can re-publish the same anomaly, always with the SAME event_id, so consumers de-duplicate on event_id like every other topic. Consumers must ignore unknown fields so additive changes do not break them.

warehouse_id.description: Canonical warehouse id (city IATA code), e.g. WH-BLR-01.

date.description: Sales day of the anomaly, YYYY-MM-DD. For a run of anomalous days this is the first day.

expected_quantity.description: Units the detector expected for that day: the median of the same weekday over the previous 8 weeks.

actual_quantity.description: Units actually sold that day, summed over all rows for the product and warehouse. 0 when the warehouse reported other products that day but none of this one.

score.description: Robust z-score of the day: (actual - expected) / noise scale. Positive for a spike, negative for a drop. Drops are judged by their share of the expected quantity, so a drop can have a small negative score.

severity.description: Producer-assigned urgency, ordered low < medium < high. Treat it as an ordered label only; the exact rule is owned by the anomaly service.
